<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Carefully designing the migration to avoid circular dependencies.

Mapping the current import chain reveals a circular dependency risk. `pipeline.ts` imports `analyzeWithRules` from `analyzer.ts`, while `analyzer.ts` currently imports `Pipeline` from `pipeline.ts` for its thin facade. This cross-reference must be resolved during the migration.

The dependency cycle extends through `fixer.ts` too. `pipeline.ts` imports `fixFileWithRules` from `fixer.ts`, while `fixer.ts` imports `Pipeline` from `pipeline.ts` for its facade. Evaluating structural fixes like moving shared types or reorganizing facade exports to break the loop.

The chosen fix is to import only leaf functions from analyzer and fixer into pipeline.ts. Facades in those files will import Pipeline instead. ES modules allow circular imports when references are used at call time rather than at module initialization.

Option B would break existing tests that import analyzeFiles directly. Option C risks the same circular dependency. Proceeding with Option A: pipeline.ts will import the leaf functions directly and own the end-to-end loops. Facades in analyzer and fixer will import Pipeline from pipeline.ts. Bun and TypeScript handle these circular references safely at call time.

Checking whether the codebase already uses a pattern for top-level circular imports between pipeline and analyzer. Inline imports are ruled out by the no-inline-imports constraint.

A cleaner structural fix is emerging. Moving `PipelineResult` and `FixFilesOptions` into `pipeline.ts` would eliminate the need for `fixer.ts` to import `Pipeline` back from `pipeline.ts`. `processOneFile` and the main loop would also move into `pipeline.ts`. This removes the circular dependency entirely without relying on call-time circular imports.

Facades will delegate to Pipeline.run with mode arguments: analyze for analyzer.analyzeFiles, fix for fixer.runPipeline and fixer.fixFiles. Top-level circular imports are safe because Pipeline.run is accessed only at call time. The createUnfixedResult helper will either stay in fixer and be exported, or be duplicated minimally in pipeline.

`processOneFile` depends on `service.parseFile`, `analyzeWithRules`, `fixFileWithRules`, file I/O, and `createUnfixedResult`. The tiny `createUnfixedResult` helper will be inlined directly into `pipeline.ts` rather than exported from `fixer.ts`.

`Pipeline.run` will unify the two existing entry points. It resolves files, enables rules, then iterates over each file to parse and analyze. The existing analyze-only loop and the full analyze-fix loop will both collapse into this single orchestration body.

Pipeline.run will branch on a mode argument. Analyze mode forces fix: false. Fix mode forces fix: true. This prevents empty fix result arrays when callers omit the flag. Pipeline currently requires fileService from callers. The unified loop must supply it itself.

Facades will instantiate a default FileService internally. Drafting the new pipeline.ts interface now: PipelineResult, PipelineMode, and direct imports from analyzer, fixer, registry, and services.

Drafting the `PipelineRunOptions` interface now. It carries patterns, config, fileService, registry, mode, resolvedFiles, and dryRun. The `Pipeline.run` implementation begins by destructuring these options, resolving files from patterns if none were supplied, and fetching the enabled rules from the registry.

The `Pipeline.run` loop is now fully drafted. It iterates over resolved files, delegates each path to `processOneFile`, and accumulates `analysisResults` and `fixResults`. The `shouldFix` flag controls whether fix results are collected. The method returns a single `PipelineResult` object containing both arrays.

Drafting the analyzer facade now. It instantiates a default FileService when none is provided, then delegates to Pipeline.run with mode set to "analyze" and fix forced to false. The fixer facade is next.

The fixer facade is now fully drafted. `runPipeline` instantiates a default `FileService` and delegates to `Pipeline.run` with mode set to `"fix"` and `fix` forced to `true`. `fixFiles` simply calls `runPipeline` and returns the extracted `fixResults`.

`PipelineResult` will move into `pipeline.ts` and be re-exported from `fixer.ts` for backward compatibility. `FixFilesOptions` stays in `fixer.ts` because `cli-runners` imports it directly. The pipeline stub documentation needs updating. `pipeline.test.ts` should track the "Fixed" stage explicitly for fix mode, since `fixFileWithRules` bypasses `FileService` writes during `dryRun`.

The test should verify the "Fixed" stage in fix mode, since dryRun skips actual file writes. A test asserting fixResults when mode is "fix" is planned. Package exports for analyzeFiles and runPipeline also need checking.
</details></think>
